title.narrative: Improving access to lifesaving anticipatory action WASH services for projected La Niña and drought-affected vulnerable populations in Afmadow district

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe 2024 HNRP anticipates severe deprivation in most regions, with around 6.9 million people needing humanitarian aid. Global weather forecasts suggest a 70% likelihood of La Niña conditions, likely resulting in hotter, drier weather and below-average rainfall, especially in south-central Somalia. This will likely exacerbate acute malnutrition, food insecurity, and water shortages, precipitating displacement and worsening disease outbreaks. The La Niña mitigation, preparedness, and response plan indicates that more than half of the affected population will face water insecurity, worsening during the 2025 Jiilaal season. Water scarcity will compel communities to use unsafe water sources, heightening the risk of waterborne diseases and potentially causing a public health crisis. An MRNA in Afmadow district in August 2024 showed that only 40% of conflict-affected households have sufficient, safe water, and 45% lack functioning sanitation facilities. A WASH gap and priorities analysis from the same period revealed that the last Gu rains destroyed six shallow wells in Afmadow town, and over 8,000 households, mainly IDPs, lack sanitation facilities. The district is classified as a priority district with a severity level of 4 and contains numerous hard-to-reach, underserved rural villages.. The project aims to provide early action integrated critical WASH services to the most vulnerable people in Afmadow district.ltbrgtTo reduce the impact of climatic shocks and prevent waterborne diseases, the project will deliver WASH services to 20,000 people, including those affected by climatic shocks, at risk of cholera, displaced without basic sanitation, and users of nutrition and healthcare facilities in Afmadow District. SRDI will implement life-saving WASH interventions targeting 20,000 individuals in Afmadow. To ensure integration and synergy with other sector interventions, SRDI will coordinate closely with Alight, which provides health and nutrition services, and other regional actors to prevent duplication and resource wastage.ltbrgtThe following are the summary of the proposed activities by SRDI:ltbrgt Rehabilitation, protection, and upgrading of two strategic shallow wells in Afmadow town, including the construction of a 20 cubic meter elevated tank and installation of a solar pumping system.ltbrgt Rehabilitation and equipping of two strategic boreholes in Dhobley town (Guxweyne and Dhobale), which includes replacing the submersible pump (15 KW) and installing a generator for the Dhobale borehole.ltbrgt Piped Water Extension:ltbrgto Extension of a 4 km piped water system to two IDP camps and construction of four water kiosks. Camp Midnimo in Dhobley and Bula Gumar camp in Afmadow townltbrgt Training of 24 WASH committee members on water point management.ltbrgt Conducting water quality monitoring and routine chlorination of five water points.ltbrgt Construction of Latrines: Construction of 18 gender-sensitive, disability-friendly communal latrines for disaster-affected rural populations and IDPs in targeted areas of Afmadow. Construction of 150 emergency communal latrines.ltbrgto Purchase and distribution of 80 sanitation tool kits.ltbrgt Conducting 18 clean-up campaigns throughout the duration of the project in five target sites.ltbrgt Purchase and distribution of 1,000 hygiene kits for vulnerable beneficiaries. Overal Project target locations are Dobley ( Midnimo IDP camp,, Waaberi and Danwadaag IDP camp) Afmadow town ( Bula Gumar IDP camp) and Dacas village .ltbrgt - Conducting extensive hygiene promotion activities, including 24 sessions led by hygiene promoters trained on AWD/cholera prevention.ltbrgtThe suite of activities addresses both immediate and long-term needs of vulnerable IDP communities and fosters relationships for ongoing maintenance and operation. SRDI WASH technical designs comply with SPHERE standards and Somalia WASH cluster guidelines, incorporating protection, disability, and gender considerations as outlined by IASC guidelines for GBV Interventions in Humanitarian settings.ltbrgtlt/pgt
